title: Prepare and deliver private job application packets
summary: Prepare private job briefs and tailored resumes, or use one configured PDF for daily emails. Freeze editions and send retained attachment bytes through authorized runs.
use_when: The user wants to prepare or preview eligible Cast opportunities with a concise brief and a constrained resume.
The user wants an explicitly authorized send or another edition composed from retained materials.
The user wants to change job eligibility or export a retained artifact to an explicit destination.
The user has authorized daily email and wants one invocation to prepare, freeze and send the current local-date edition.
The user explicitly wants one supplied public job URL prepared and emailed to the fixed personal recipient.
The user wants another packet for a previously prepared job, including one already used in an edition, without re-enabling it or sending email.
The user wants to replace the fixed resume template for future preparations while retaining earlier templates and packets.
The user wants to set or clear one static PDF override for future daily email resumes.
do_not_use_when: The request is job discovery, source-library editing, employer outreach or application submission.
The caller expects stored delivery settings or installation alone to enable a schedule, or expects preparation to change fixed content outside its editable regions.
outcome: Stored private job briefs and either tailored resumes or one shared PDF for a daily edition. Preview freezes selected packets and attachments; authorized send records provider acceptance.

effects: Initialization/import/configuration selects private future material without preparing or sending. Explicit export creates a new private file.

Preparation captures source material and can consume Nucleus/Weaver allowance. Normal repetition continues saved work; an explicitly authorized fresh restart or regeneration creates its supported new capture.

Ordinary preview checks freshness, freezes exact material, and spends selected job eligibility. Retained-material preview freezes the same representation without changing eligibility or calling preparation dependencies.

An applicable authorized send records sending before Email and acceptance afterward. Daily/URL-selected run commands may prepare and freeze before that send under one mutation lock. Definition printing starts no schedule.
authority: Platter owns captured inputs, content validation, explicit job eligibility, edition identity and delivery state. Nucleus owns execution and tool-call history.

Weaver authors project bullets. Platter owns fixed presentation, Markdown conversion, at most three bullets per project and mechanical acceptance. Its draft agent writes only brief and Jackson; its toolset cannot submit project fields. Historical runs retain their original boundaries.

Each send requires applicable user authority. Explicit authorization to enable recurring daily email supplies standing authority for ordinary daily briefs and resume attachments to the fixed personal recipient. Invoking run-ad-hoc is one explicit send instruction for its selected URL and occurrence. Preparation, preview, catalog presence and model output grant no send authority.
success: Verify the retained packet readiness or expected decline/deferral outcome defined by platter.preparation.
Verify preview's exact frozen selection and message without sending.
Verify retained recognized Email acceptance or the no-edition outcome; provider acceptance does not prove inbox receipt or an application.
failure_and_recovery: Stop for unsupported state, failed prerequisites, foreign holds, incomplete source reads, invalid template/PDF, or preparation failure. Preserve accepted artifacts and exact requests.

Normal repetition resumes retained work. A terminal failure receives no automatic replacement or direct Codex fallback. --fresh and regeneration require their feature-defined terminal-job and capture preconditions.
Posting retrieval failure marks a job ineligible; daily work can try another candidate. Other preparation/export errors stop before sending.
Exact frozen/accepted/uncertain occurrences use platter.editions: do not create replacement payloads or send keys to bypass held uncertainty.
Repair the exact renderer/source/runtime failure before an authorized new attempt. Use platter.install.operate for maintained schema backup/migration; do not edit SQLite.
Clockwork continuation permits only future scheduling and preserves Platter preparation/delivery recovery.
privacy: Private state includes career history, preferences, contact details, source text and tailored resumes. Keep it outside the repository and exclude it from commits.

Nucleus and the model receive career and posting inputs for Platter, and selected Annals decisions for Weaver. Platter retains Weaver Markdown, not its source reads. Authorized sends disclose only their frozen message and attachments through Email.
does_not_authorize: Installing or enabling any scheduled activation.
Sending when the user requested only preparation or preview.
Changing fixed resume content, modifying Vita or Cast outside run-ad-hoc's exact URL collection, applying to a job or contacting an employer.

consumers.statement: The current user or an explicitly authorized local caller uses supported Platter CLI preparation, selection, export, and send procedures.

preconditions.statement: Use canonical schema-seven state and the required source/runtime/template or daily-PDF prerequisites declared by platter.materials and platter.preparation. Retained-only selection needs completed material and makes no source/model/rendering calls. Each send needs applicable authority and Email --payload-stdin.
New prompt preparation needs initialized private Bazaar state and a complete cell.prompts.platter selection; runtime neither creates state nor uses fallback text.

inputs.statement: Select a Cast job, daily pool, exact public URL, or retained complete packets. Supply exact regeneration/occurrence identities and applicable explicit template, PDF, brief-override, export, and deadline inputs. Required features own their formats and meaning.

outputs.statement: Preparation reports retained run status and artifact identities; preview freezes an edition; an applicable authorized send reports retained acceptance or unresolved uncertainty. Exports write new private files. Run output is compact and omits body/PDF bytes. Detailed record meaning belongs to required features.

data_semantics.statement: Use platter.preparation for eligibility, current/historical workflows, and readiness. Use platter.materials for captured and accepted bytes, templates, settings, and export. Use platter.editions for independent selected packet/attachment identity and submission acceptance.

identity_and_units.statement: Retain the exact selected job, run, regeneration request, edition occurrence, and send key. Apply the compatible identity/units rules in required features; another deliberately changed capture or frozen payload needs its appropriate new identity.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Before new work, apply required source capture, complete Vita reads, posting-cache freshness, and exact retained-occurrence rules. Existing frozen editions use retained bytes; retained-material selection refreshes no source. Required features own coverage and timestamps.

access.statement: Use canonical current-user Platter interfaces under normal mutation admission. Preparation permissions and Weaver source authority are defined by platter.preparation; sending uses Email's existing credential and fixed recipient.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Retain exact captured requests and occurrence identity. Repetition continues saved work; terminal failures get no automatic replacement. Ordinary preview freezes and spends eligibility atomically, sending intent precedes transport, and uncertain/accepted occurrences follow platter.editions without a new send key.

operational_limits.statement: Apply required feature limits and supported deadlines. Daily preparation has no candidate/token budget; editions permit at most three packets and URL-selected occurrences one. No installation or stored time field activates recurring work.
No preparation-latency, completion-time, delivery-time or throughput guarantee exists. Activation is a separately authorized Clockwork operation; stored 09:00 fields do not control it.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Keep the existing operation ID/version, supported commands, and exact historical input/output/delivery meaning. Required features define current and historical generation, template, state, and prompt compatibility.

No arbitrary incompatible rollback, model support interval or deprecation window is promised. Full-template and projects-only imports select templates for future captures; historical captures retain their exact template references.

reliances.statement: Retained job evidence and stable discovery IDs come from Cast supported exports.
URL-selected runs rely on Cast to resolve or collect one supplied public posting into its normal job records.
Career entries are the complete retained works in the fixed Annals vita library, read through ~/.local/bin/annals work list/show in named-library scope.
Constrained execution, authentication and durable requester-tool transport rely on Nucleus.
Explicit fixed-recipient submission with local attachments relies on Email contract 4.
Full posting retrieval depends on employer HTTPS sources and their supported ATS or JobPosting representations.
PDF generation depends on locally available LaTeX, fonts and PDF inspection executables.

The product-owned schema-two definition declares halt-until-approved. Clockwork owns activation, the shared service-health delay before a new durable halt, incident email and exact continuation approval; Platter owns expected readiness outcomes, date selection and preserved preparation/delivery recovery.
Historical project-authoring agents use Annals concept search, evidence and retained works under their frozen instructions.

Historical preparations that retain repository resource instructions depend on those local directories being readable by the selected Nucleus harness. Platter provides no repository snapshots or availability guarantee.
Weaver authors private project Markdown through its typed installed CLI client, with caller-supplied identity and exact-request recovery. It owns its Annals reads and Nucleus jobs.
Bazaar supplies immutable text versions. The caller owns selection JSON, rendering, permissions, and execution; a string supplies no additional authority.

session_surfaces: private Platter state and explicit input/output files
steps: Inspect canonical state and dependency readiness; select preparation, preview, or a separately authorized send.
Initialize or explicitly select supported private templates/PDF configuration when requested.
Prepare or continue the selected exact job/request, or perform an authorized fresh restart/regeneration only after its preconditions.
Freeze the intended ordinary or retained-material selection and inspect the retained result.
Send only the applicable authorized occurrence and verify retained acceptance or held uncertainty.
Use supported source/prompt/activation operations separately, preserving exact historical work and external halts.
checkpoints: Canonical schema-seven state and required source/runtime/material prerequisites are established.
Any send has applicable direct or standing authority; preview alone supplies none.
Preparation is accepted by Platter rather than inferred from Nucleus completion.
The exact frozen selection/body/attachment identity and send outcome are retained.
adaptation: Use tailored single-job/regeneration/URL-selected work or supported daily PDF brief work as intended; do not continue a packet through the wrong workflow.
Use retained-material selection when no source/model/rendering work is intended.
Preserve the original request or occurrence on interruption; an explicit genuinely new capture or payload uses its supported new identity.
stop_when: State, prerequisite, template/PDF, source completeness, maintenance ownership, or required authorization cannot be established.
A terminal model failure needs another attempt outside already authorized fresh/regeneration scope.
A send is uncertain, an occurrence conflicts with its saved input, or source/renderer/runtime failure remains unresolved.
A requested change would require source-library writes, employer contact, application submission, or clearing unrelated holds/halts.
